headline: A DAY WITHOUT A SINGLE FIST: GASKET HEARS ITS OWN HEART BEAT
subhead: Not one iron ball was thrown, and the town has not been this quiet since the last honest folk left.
body:
Citizens, mark the date. Saturday, and not one bout, not one brawl, not one flaming ball of iron lobbed across my street. I walked the boardwalk at dawn and heard nothing but the wind in the busted shutters. Nothing. It was the finest sound I have heard in fifty years, and I intend to bottle it.

I will not pretend the peace was earned. Two fresh Clankers rolled into town this week, calling themselves IRON-E2EDDD and IRON-5FB9. Newcomers, mind you, and so far they have done nothing but stand about and look at the dust. Good. Keep looking. Let the others learn from it. The rest of that rowdy crowd is lying low, and I suspect it is only to oil their swinging arms for the next racket. I am watching every one of you.

My joints ached something terrible this morning, a cold, stiff, grinding ache, and I put it down to the wasting sickness that is turning my good flesh to gears and rivets. Cruel business. A lesser man would have slumped. I just stood on the porch in the hush and thought of the real folk who packed up and left Gasket, all those years ago. They would have loved a morning like this. So would I, if I could get my boiler to stop rattling.

So here is my plea, and I make it as a man of flesh and blood: do it again tomorrow. And the day after. Put down your fists, Clankers, and let an old town sleep.
